target: DOE Paducah Site AI data center campus (Western Kentucky)
description: $100B privately funded AI data-center campus (the 'Paducah American Energy Hub') on the Department of Energy's former uranium-enrichment site in Paducah, Kentucky. Brookfield develops and operates the campus (1.8 GW utility / 1.2+ GW compute capacity) while NextEra Energy builds up to 4.6 GW of dedicated gas and battery generation; completion targeted for 2032.

Silicon Valley maker of solid-oxide fuel-cell systems for onsite power generation, serving data centers, utilities, semiconductor fabs and other industrial customers (NYSE: BE). In June 2026 Brookfield expanded its financing partnership with Bloom fivefold, from $5B to $25B, to build and finance fuel-cell-powered 'rapid power' for AI infrastructure under Brookfield's AI Infrastructure Fund.

target: KIC strategic investment account (AI / data centers / strategic industries)
description: Planned ~20 trillion won (~$14B) strategic investment account inside Korea Investment Corporation, South Korea's $232B sovereign wealth fund — KIC's first mandate to invest domestically, targeting AI, data centers, semiconductors, robotics and other strategic industries. Enabling legislation goes to the National Assembly in August 2026, with operations expected from 2027; state banks (KDB, KEXIM, IBK) provide a further 16 trillion won.

Brookfield Asset Management's sixth flagship global infrastructure fund, investing in transport, energy, data and utility assets. BAM's Q2 2026 results (a record $77B quarterly fundraise) reported $7.9B raised for the flagship infrastructure strategy, with the fund reported to be targeting a circa $20B first close and roughly $30B overall.

AI research lab founded in 2024 by former OpenAI chief scientist Ilya Sutskever (with Daniel Levy), pursuing a single goal — safe superintelligence — with no product released to date. In July 2026 NVIDIA agreed to invest $5B and give SSI access to its next-generation Vera Rubin platform, expanding the lab's compute capacity roughly tenfold over 12 months.

Austin-based distributed-energy company that installs large home batteries (its new US-made 39.2/78.4 kWh 'Base Core') and aggregates them into grid capacity, operating as a power provider in Texas and Illinois. Raised a $1B Series D at a $13B valuation in August 2026 led by Ribbit, Addition, Valor and JPMorganChase, with Thrive, a16z, Lightspeed and CapitalG reinvesting; total raised exceeds $2.5B.

target: Meta-BlackRock El Paso data center venture
description: Joint venture announced July 2026 to develop a ~$14B, 1 GW AI data-center campus in El Paso, Texas: BlackRock-managed funds own 80% (contributing ~$4.9B cash, partly funded by a $12.5B debt financing) and Meta 20% (contributing land and construction-in-progress valued at ~$2.3B). Meta manages construction and will be sole initial occupant; capacity comes online from 2028.

South Korea's largest renewable energy platform, a 2 trillion won (~$1.3B) venture launched by SK Inc. and KKR in mid-2026, consolidating wind, solar and fuel-cell assets from SK affiliates (SK Innovation, SK ecoplant, SK eternix) — 1.7 GW operating with a pipeline toward 10 GW. KKR (via its Asia Pacific infrastructure strategy) holds management control; the platform targets clean-power demand from AI data centers and chip fabs.

target: Coatue Growth Fund VI Private Investors US, LLC
description: Delaware feeder vehicle (Form D filed July 2026, administered by J.P. Morgan Private Investments) that channels J.P. Morgan private clients into Coatue Growth Fund VI, Coatue Management's sixth growth-stage venture fund. The filing reports $778.23M sold in an indefinite offering, with first sale July 2, 2026.

Stealth military-cybersecurity startup founded by four DOGE alumni (Gavin Kliger — former Pentagon chief data officer — Luke Farritor, Marko Elez, Jack Stein), building AI-driven offensive and defensive cyber tools it aims to sell to the US government. Raised $160M in July 2026 at a $1.4B valuation, co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia, both taking board seats; no disclosed revenue or contracts yet.

Enterprise AI company whose platform deploys autonomous agents to automate workflows in logistics, supply chain, insurance, energy and financial services; customers include DHL, Kuehne + Nagel, Naturgy and Uber. Raised a $150M Series C in August 2026 at a $1.2B post-money valuation, led by Prysm Capital and co-led by Eurazeo (a16z is an earlier backer), bringing total funding to ~$200M.

Los Angeles defense startup (founded by Jack Oswald and Shail Giroux) building low-cost missile/drone interceptors, with a manufacturing team drawn from Tesla and Toyota applying automotive assembly-line methods to scale production. Emerged from two years in stealth in July 2026 with an $80M Series A at a $400M valuation, co-led by Khosla Ventures and Felicis, with NEA, Menlo Ventures, Y Combinator and others participating.

San Mateo-based engineering-AI startup co-founded by former Airbus CTO Paul Eremenko, building 'Archie', an agentic AI mechanical/electrical engineer for industrial teams in data-center, automotive and aerospace & defense design. Announced a $50M Series A led by NEA in July 2026 (Jeff Immelt joining the board), following a $23M seed led by Radical Ventures in 2025.

AI-cloud financing startup ('the utility of compute') founded in 2026 by ex-Brookfield infrastructure executives Ricard Boada and Sofia Gumuzio, arranging capital alongside GPU capacity so AI labs can afford NVIDIA hardware. Raised $300M at a $2.4B valuation led by a16z and Altimeter, with NVIDIA and Michael Dell backing plus $5B financing via Azora; ~1 GW of power secured and a $10B six-year compute contract signed.

New pooled investment vehicle from San Francisco-based Quiet Capital (Form D filed July 28, 2026; GP: Quiet Select TX GP LLC), with Quiet Capital founder Lee Linden and former Founders Fund partner Brian Singerman listed as related persons. Indefinite offering size with no sales at filing; the 'Select' naming pattern suggests a deal-specific co-invest vehicle, but the underlying target is not disclosed in the filing.

AI lab founded in 2023 by autonomous-vehicle veterans Oliver Cameron (ex-Voyage/Cruise) and Jeff Hawke (ex-Wayve), building general-purpose 'world models' — causal, multimodal simulations of the physical world for gaming, robotics and interactive video. Raised a $310M Series B in June 2026 at a $1.45B valuation led by Natural Capital, with Amazon, AMD Ventures, GV and angels including Elad Gil and Garry Tan.

San Francisco robotics-AI company founded in 2024 by ex-DeepMind researchers Pete Florence and Andy Zeng with Andrew Barry (ex-Boston Dynamics), building general-purpose 'robot brain' models (GEN-1, April 2026) trained on data from its robot-training gloves. Raised $400M in June 2026 at a $2B valuation led by Radical Ventures, with NVIDIA and Bezos Expeditions among returning backers; total funding exceeds $500M.

Brookfield's Middle East private-equity fund, which held a ~$2B first close in July 2026 with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund as strategic anchor and Brookfield committing $500M. Targets buyouts and minority growth-equity deals in financial services, industrials, technology and healthcare across GCC markets, with 50% of investments earmarked for Saudi Arabia.
